source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Harness design: before solving, the model gives a feeling-of-knowing (FOK) score in [0,1] with no reasoning allowed. After each attempt it gives a judgment-of-learning (JOL) score. A per-model SVM on (FOK, JOL) decides stop or retry. If several attempts exist, a separate aggregator picks one existing attempt.
numbers: Fixed solver Claude Sonnet-4.6. SVM poly d=3, isotonic calibration, stop threshold p=0.7, fitted on a 100-problem anchor set disjoint from test data. Text, code and multimodal tasks.
limits: Code, prompts and data are promised for later, not in the text read. The controller is fitted on only 100 items.
agent_relevance: Direct template for S0 gate and S6 impasse trigger: monitoring is a score read by code, and code decides retry or stop. Fits G1 (doubt only on a signal) if the signal is validated.

source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Headline result at the pooled level. Harness beats single pass and four other test-time baselines.
numbers: Pooled 1,859 questions (HLE-Verified 668, LiveCodeBench v6 388, R-Bench-V 803). Pass@1 48.3, harness 56.9 (+8.6). Self-Refine 52.4 (1.5 attempts, $0.45/q). Budget forcing 51.5 ($0.67). Verifier reranking 49.8 (4.0 attempts, $1.32). Aggregator 53.7 (4.0 attempts, $1.42). Harness: 2.4 attempts, $0.78/q. Pass@1 cost $0.29/q.
limits: Not equal compute: harness cost is about 2.7x pass@1. No plain best-of-2.4 or majority vote at the same dollar cost is given. Authors say 'matched or comparable'. Single run, single base model. Leaderboard comparison mixes models and reasoning settings.
agent_relevance: Confirms the 48.3 to 56.9 figure from the paper itself. Supports G12 (spend by difficulty). G7 is not yet satisfied: no equal-token plain baseline.

source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Per-benchmark gains. Biggest gain is on hard code problems.
numbers: HLE-Verified Gold 48.0 to 60.0 (+12.0). LiveCodeBench overall 74.3 to 84.3 (+10.0); Easy 95.4 to 94.7 (-0.7); Medium +1.1; Hard 55.0 to 74.6 (+19.6). R-Bench-V overall 36.1 to 41.1 (+5.0).
limits: Table text was garbled by PDF extraction; row alignment read by position and checked against the stated gains.
agent_relevance: Gain concentrates where the model is unsure. Matches G12: a foothold is needed. Easy items show no gain, a small loss.

source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Ablation on a 100-question subset. Every removed part lowers accuracy, but all intervals overlap.
numbers: Pass@1 44.0, Oracle@4 53.0. Full harness 47.0 [37,57], K=2.58, early-stop hit 76.7%. Without FOK 45.0; without JOL 42.0; hand rule (1-JOL)xFOK 42.0 (K=2.40); random retry at matched K 45.7 [43,48]; last answer of 4: 40.0; max-JOL of 4: 44.0; no prior metacognitive state 45.0; full previous reasoning in context 40.0.
limits: N=100, 95% bootstrap CIs span about 20 points. Full harness (47.0) vs random retry at same K (45.7) is a 1.3 point gap, far inside noise. The ablation does not by itself prove directed retry beats random retry.
agent_relevance: Key caution for G7. The directed-retry claim is weak at this sample size. We must run our own equal-token test with random retry as a control.

source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Where the gain comes from: low-confidence problems. High-confidence problems get no gain.
numbers: Accuracy by first-attempt JOL band: low 0.16 to 0.42; medium 0.36 to 0.55; high 0.67 to 0.64 (slight loss). Attempts fall monotonically from low to high confidence.
limits: Bands are defined by the same JOL that drives control. Some regression to the mean is possible in the low band.
agent_relevance: Supports G1 and G12: retry only when the signal says low confidence. Confident-but-wrong answers are not rescued, which is the real risk.

source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Confidence is for allocating effort across problems, not for choosing among attempts on one problem. The authors hide FOK/JOL from the aggregator.
numbers: Median within-problem SD of JOL 0.048; across-problem SD 0.270 (about 5.6x wider). Max-JOL selection (44.0) was worse than the full harness aggregator (47.0, N=100).
limits: The aggregator is itself an LLM judge that sees reasoning and answers; no test of self-preference.
agent_relevance: Agrees with G5 and G4: samples from one model share confidence. Use confidence to gate, never to rank. Selection still needs code checks.

source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Retry context: pass only a compact history (previous answer, JOL, one-line reason for the JOL), not the old reasoning. Full old reasoning anchors the model on its errors.
numbers: Full previous reasoning 40.0 vs compact feedback 47.0 vs no prior state 45.0 (N=100, CIs overlap). Self-Refine, which shows full derivations, got 52.4 vs harness 56.9 on the full set.
limits: The 2-point gap between compact and no-state is inside noise. The anchoring effect (about 7 points) is larger but also uncertain.
agent_relevance: Design rule for S5 REVISE: show the failing output and the stated doubt, not the full prior chain. Consistent with G2.

source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Metacognitive diagnosis across nine models. Many models have discriminative confidence but few are calibrated. Only Sonnet-4.6 passes every row of the rubric.
numbers: Anchor N=100. Sonnet-4.6 (accuracy 0.58): FOK AUROC 0.612, JOL AUROC 0.745, joint AUROC 0.757, joint ECE 0.087. Gemini-3-Flash (accuracy 0.34): FOK AUROC 0.818 but raw ECE 0.465 (FOK) and 0.528 (JOL). Gemma 4 (accuracy 0.19): FOK AUROC 0.534 (fail), raw ECE about 0.47 to 0.52. Thresholds: AUROC >= 0.60, ECE <= 0.15.
limits: With N=100, an AUROC of 0.61 barely clears 0.60 and has a wide interval. The harness was run end to end only on the model that passed. Authors admit it is not model-universal.
agent_relevance: Before trusting any confidence gate, run a small diagnosis on our own base model. A gate fitted on 100 items is a placeholder [D], not a result.

source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Without the harness, the model does not spend more effort on problems where it is unsure, even though its confidence predicts correctness. The harness fixes this by external control.
numbers: Figure 1: higher FOK/JOL bands have higher accuracy; reasoning length does not consistently rise for low-confidence items across the nine models (arrow counts in appendix A).
limits: Reasoning length is a crude proxy for effort. Shown as arrow counts, not a significance test.
agent_relevance: Argues that monitoring must sit in code outside the model (our section 1), since the model alone does not act on its own doubt.

source: Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Stated limitations and planned work.
numbers: Authors: effectiveness depends on base-model signals being discriminative and calibratable; controller fitted on a small anchor set may fail under distribution shift; no long-horizon agent tests yet.
limits: Agent benchmarks, MCP/Skill packaging and code release are future work.
agent_relevance: No evidence yet that the harness helps in multi-step agent loops. Treat as single source [S].

source: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Self-correction with an oracle label gains a lot. Without the oracle (intrinsic self-correction) it gets worse. The oracle tells the model when not to change a right answer; that is the hidden help.
numbers: With oracle: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 89.7, HotpotQA 26.0 to 29.0; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5, CSQA 82.0 to 85.5, HotpotQA 49 to 59. Intrinsic, GPT-4: GSM8K 95.5, 91.5 (round 1), 89.0 (round 2); HotpotQA 49, 49, 43. GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 to 38.1 then 41.8.
quote: the improvements vanish when oracle labels are not available
limits: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 era models, 2023. Reasoning-trained models may differ. Table rows were garbled in extraction and read by position.
agent_relevance: Core support for G2 and G6. A gate that decides when to stop revising is the missing oracle. Cao's harness tries to approximate that oracle with a learned confidence rule.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (multi-agent debate section)
finding: Multi-agent debate gains are mostly extra sampling. At equal numbers of responses, plain self-consistency beats debate.
numbers: GSM8K, as read from the table: debate with 9 responses 83.0 vs self-consistency with 9 responses 88.2; debate with 3 responses about 83.2 vs self-consistency 3 responses 82.5.
limits: Math reasoning only; GPT-3.5. Table partly garbled.
agent_relevance: Supports G9 (no debate) with equal-compute evidence.

source: Kamoi, Zhang, Zhang, Han, Zhang (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
finding: Survey of self-correction work to May 2024. No prior work shows successful self-correction with feedback from a prompted LLM, except tasks unusually suited to it. Self-correction works with reliable external feedback. Large-scale fine-tuning enables it.
numbers: Three conclusions as stated in the abstract. The survey also gives a checklist for fair experiments and finds many papers use unfair setups (oracle labels, weak baselines).
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
limits: Survey, no new experiments. Cut off at May 2024, before reasoning models and before Cao et al. (2026).
agent_relevance: The 2026 harness claims its gain comes from a calibrated gate plus directed retry. The survey says check that the baseline is fair and that feedback is not an oracle. Cao uses no oracle, but the retry feedback is the model's own text.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Larger models are well calibrated on multiple choice and true/false in the right format. P(True) self-evaluation of a proposed answer works and improves when the model sees many of its own samples. A trained P(IK) predictor works but calibration fails on new tasks.
numbers: Abstract and contents read; exact AUC numbers not recorded.
quote: Models perform well at predicting P(IK) and partially generalize across tasks
limits: Models up to 52B, calibration shown mostly on multiple-choice formats. P(IK) needs training. RLHF policy calibration needed temperature tuning.
agent_relevance: Origin of the FOK idea in LLM form (P(IK) is a pre-answer signal, P(True) is post-answer). Cao's FOK/JOL prompts are zero-shot versions of these.

source: Xiong, Hu, Lu, Li, Fu, He, Hooi (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
finding: Verbalized confidence is overconfident and a weak failure predictor. Human-inspired prompts and consistency among samples help, but no strategy wins everywhere. Professional-knowledge tasks stay hard.
numbers: Verbalized values mostly 80 to 100%. GPT-4 vanilla verbalized confidence: average AUROC 62.7% (near 50% chance). AUROC gain GPT-3 to GPT-4 about 22.2%. White-box vs black-box gap 0.522 to 0.605 AUROC. Five LLMs, eight tasks.
quote: LLMs, when verbalizing their confidence, tend to be overconfident
limits: 2023 models. Later models are better (Sonnet-4.6 joint AUROC 0.757 in Cao). Prompt choice changes results, no consistent winner.
agent_relevance: Prior art for why a raw confidence number cannot gate by a fixed threshold. Calibrate first, as Cao does with an isotonic SVM.

source: Xiong et al. (2024) Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? (prompt strategy section)
finding: Multi-step confidence, top-K guesses and human-inspired wording each reduce overconfidence a little, with diminishing returns for GPT-4. No single strategy is best on all datasets and models.
numbers: Five prompting strategies compared on five datasets with GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
limits: Gains described as modest; per-strategy numbers are in figures that were not read.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a prompt tweak fixes calibration. Fit the gate on data.

source: Wang and Zhao (2024) Metacognitive Prompting Improves Understanding in Large Language Models
finding: Metacognitive Prompting (MP) is a fixed multi-stage prompt: understand the text, make a first judgment, critically evaluate it, give the final decision with explanation, then rate confidence. It beats CoT and plan-and-solve on language understanding tasks.
numbers: Ten NLU datasets, four models (Llama2, PaLM2, GPT-3.5, GPT-4). Zero-shot MP relative gain over CoT 4.8% to 6.4%, over PS 2.8% to 4.1%. Averaged over models: QQP acc 87.3 vs CoT 85.9; BoolQ 89.0 vs 86.3; MedNLI 70.9 vs 67.1. Gains over PS: MedNLI 4.3%, UNFAIR-ToS 9.6%, EUR-LEX 12.4%.
limits: Understanding tasks, not hard reasoning. Single-pass script with no code-level gate. Token cost not compared with CoT-SC at equal tokens. The fixed self-doubt step runs on every item, which conflicts with G1.
agent_relevance: The prompt-only kind of metacognition. It differs from Cao: it always runs the self-critique. G1 and our word-puzzle data (92% plain vs 75% with forced doubt) warn against it.

source: Didolkar, Goyal, Ke, Guo, Valko, Lillicrap, Rezende, Bengio, Mozer, Arora (2024) Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: An Exploration in Mathematical Problem Solving
finding: GPT-4 names the skill needed for each math question and clusters labels into coarse skills (117 for MATH). At test time the model picks the skill, then receives same-skill solved examples. This is metacognitive knowledge used as retrieval.
numbers: MATH: 11.6% enhancement over CoT; code-based (PAL) solutions +7.52%. The MATH repository also helps weaker LLMs; the GSM8K repository helps other math datasets.
limits: Relative enhancements, not absolute points in the text read. Math only. Needs a training set of solved problems.
agent_relevance: Maps to S0 (look up the problem class) and operator choice. Cheap and has no self-doubt step. Test at equal tokens.

source: Jiang, Xu, Gao et al. (2023) Active Retrieval Augmented Generation (FLARE)
finding: Uncertainty-triggered retrieval: generate the next sentence; if any token has probability below a threshold, retrieve with that sentence and regenerate. Retrieving for every sentence is not better.
numbers: 2WikiMultihopQA FLARE-direct EM 51.0, F1 59.7. Best performance when retrieval is triggered for 40% to 80% of sentences. On 2Wiki gains plateau above 60% retrieval; on StrategyQA performance drops above 50%. Average trigger rate 30% to 60% of sentences.
limits: Needs token probabilities (white box). GPT-3.5-era models. Baseline rows garbled, so only FLARE rows recorded.
agent_relevance: More retrieval or doubt is not monotonic: triggering on a signal beats always triggering. Supports G1.

source: Asai, Wu, Wang, Sil, Hajishirzi (2024) Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate and Critique through Self-Reflection
finding: A model trained to emit reflection tokens (retrieve? relevant? supported? useful?). Retrieval is adaptive, with a tunable threshold. Always retrieving the top passage hurts on some tasks.
numbers: Ablation (50k training set; PopQA, PubHealth, ASQA): 'Retrieve top 1' (always retrieve) gives a large drop on PopQA and ASQA; training without the critic or without the retriever is worse. Self-RAG beats ChatGPT on PubHealth, PopQA, biography and ASQA (Rouge, MAUVE) as reported by the authors.
limits: Requires fine-tuning, so it is not scaffold-only. Table cells garbled in extraction; no cell values copied.
agent_relevance: Training-based cousin of the harness. An adaptive 'retrieve only when needed' switch beats a fixed rule. For us the switch must be code over a validated signal (S0, S6).

source: Kapoor, Gruver, Roberts, Pal, Dooley, Goldblum, Wilson, Weller (2024) Large Language Models Must Be Taught to Know What They Don't Know
finding: Prompting alone is not enough for calibrated uncertainty. Fine-tuning on a small graded set (about 1,000 examples, LoRA) beats baselines in ECE and AUROC, generalises, and a model can estimate other models' uncertainty. A user study shows the estimates help people.
numbers: 'a thousand graded examples are sufficient to outperform baseline methods' (abstract). Exact ECE/AUROC values are in figures and not recorded.
quote: a thousand graded examples are sufficient to outperform baseline methods
limits: Needs weights or fine-tuning. Our scaffold cannot do this.
agent_relevance: Relevant to the Cao anchor set: a small graded set can fit a controller. Also a warning that prompt-only confidence has limits.

source: Li, Yuan, Feng, Pan, Wang, Sun, Wang, Li (2024) Escape Sky-High Cost: Early-Stopping Self-Consistency for Multi-Step Reasoning
finding: Knowing when to stop sampling. Draw answers in small windows and stop when a window is unanimous. Cuts samples by large margins with comparable accuracy.
numbers: Sample reduction: MATH -33.8%, GSM8K -80.1%, StrategyQA -76.8%, CommonsenseQA -78.5%, Coin Flip -84.2%, Last Letters -67.4%. Window size 5 (8 for MATH); results averaged over 10 runs.
limits: Stopping uses agreement, which is correlated across samples from one model (G4). Older models. No retry step.
agent_relevance: A code-only stop rule with no self-report: an alternative to the FOK/JOL gate that needs no calibration. Compare both at equal tokens.

source: Chen, Xu, Liang et al. (2025) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Reasoning models overspend on easy problems. Later solutions in a long chain rarely change the answer. Training to cut redundant solutions halves tokens at equal accuracy.
numbers: On '2+3': o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens than conventional models. In over 92% of cases the first round of solutions was already correct. Self-training cut tokens 48.6% on MATH500 with QwQ-32B-Preview at maintained accuracy.
limits: Open reasoning models of late 2024. The fix requires training, not a scaffold.
agent_relevance: Supports G11 (think briefly by default) and the need for an explicit stop. Cao's harness lost 0.7 points on LiveCodeBench Easy, the same pattern.

source: Chuang, Sarma, Gopalan, Boccio, Bolouki, Hu, Zhou (2025) Learning to Route LLMs with Confidence Tokens (Self-REF)
finding: Train the model to emit a confident or unconfident token after each answer, then route to a bigger model or reject when unconfident. Beats verbalized confidence and token probabilities for routing and rejection.
numbers: Tasks OpenbookQA, GSM8K, MedQA and others; routing from Llama3-8B to a larger model at several routing rates. Accuracy-versus-rate values are in figures and not recorded.
limits: Needs fine-tuning. Figure values not read.
agent_relevance: Abstain-or-escalate policy with a trained signal. For us escalate means a second attempt or an external check. G6 says never abstain on the first pass.

source: Ma, Yuan, Wang, Zhou (2025) Large Language Models Have Intrinsic Meta-Cognition, but Need a Good Lens (AutoMeco, MIRA)
finding: Benchmarks 'lenses' (perplexity, entropy, PRM-as-judge) that expose a model's awareness of step errors, and proposes MIRA, a training-free step-level reward adjustment that improves several lenses on math tasks.
numbers: Three math datasets, three LLMs. MIRA gives +5.20 and +9.20 points on one lens in two settings, while other columns fall (-7.32, -9.58). Mixed effects.
limits: Mixed results across columns; table garbled. Step-level, white-box signals.
agent_relevance: The signal source matters: internal states may monitor better than verbalized scores. Not usable in a black-box scaffold.

source: Search note on replication of Cao et al. (2026)
finding: The paper builds on Kadavath 2022, Xiong 2024, Didolkar 2024, Self-Refine, Reflexion, s1 budget forcing and Snell 2025. I found no independent replication.
numbers: Search on 2026-10-25 (WebSearch and arXiv API) returned no replication paper.
limits: Absence of a found replication is not proof that none exists.
agent_relevance: Treat 48.3 to 56.9 as a single-source claim [S]; test it ourselves at equal tokens (G7).
